evidenceGuide.meaning: Convergent evidence from replicated studies, systematic reviews or strong professional standards.
evidenceGuide.use: Use as a default design ingredient when it matches the target capability.

evidenceGuide.meaning: Good evidence with important moderators such as task, expertise, context or implementation quality.
evidenceGuide.use: Use deliberately and state the conditions required.

evidenceGuide.meaning: Promising but young, heterogeneous or technology-specific evidence.
evidenceGuide.use: Pilot, measure and retain human oversight.

evidenceGuide.meaning: Useful field-tested model without strong causal proof as a complete package.
evidenceGuide.use: Borrow the structure, but validate outcomes rather than assuming impact.
Avoid strong claims; use only with explicit caveats and measurement.

designSelector.Example options: Recall; diagnose; decide; converse; create; operate; lead
designSelector.Why it matters: Select methods by the behaviour required, not novelty.
Novices need more models and scaffolds; experts need variation and challenge.

designSelector.Example options: Retrieval; feedback; observation; generation; social learning; reflection
designSelector.Why it matters: A format works because of its mechanisms.
Protect retreat time for experiences that benefit from co-presence.
Use simulation when real practice is rare, costly or unsafe.
Design a sequence, not isolated activities.
Pilot frontier methods and measure them.

designSelector.Example options: Manager; peer pod; workflow prompt; project; coaching
designSelector.Why it matters: A retreat without transfer support usually fades.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Retrieval; spacing; successive practice; sleep and recovery
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Reverse Classroom Retreat; Capability Launch; Knowledge Expedition
mechanicsByNeed.why: Knowledge is repeatedly reconstructed over time and linked to work rather than merely encountered during the event.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Contrast and variation; interleaving; metacognitive calibration; cognitive conflict
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Executive Decision Room; Future Simulation; Ethical Dilemma Forum
mechanicsByNeed.why: Learners distinguish situations, commit to decisions, encounter challenge and inspect confidence against outcomes.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Observational learning; deliberate practice; feedback; emotion regulation
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Client Gauntlet; Negotiation Dojo; Facilitation Flight School
mechanicsByNeed.why: Expert models are followed by repeated, varied performance with specific correction and manageable stakes.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Transfer-appropriate practice; implementation intentions; habit and cue design; social accountability
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Capability Launch; Manager Transfer Lab; Peer Consultancy
mechanicsByNeed.why: Practice resembles the workplace and the environment, manager and peer system support follow-through.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Generation; productive failure; autonomy; feedback; analogical transfer
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Failure Lab; Live Challenge; Prototype Marketplace
mechanicsByNeed.why: Learners attempt, compare, receive evidence and revise, rather than being taught a single approved answer.

mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Systems War Room; Future Simulation; Observatory and Control Room
mechanicsByNeed.why: Complex relationships are externalised, manipulated and tested through consequences.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Situated learning; identity-based learning; social learning; relevance
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Learning Residency; Unconference Studio; Learning Festival
mechanicsByNeed.why: Participants contribute to an authentic practice, see credible experts and become visible members of a community.

mechanicsByNeed.mechanics: Psychological safety; error management; reflection; feedforward
mechanicsByNeed.recipes: Museum of Mistakes; Crisis Command Exercise; Failure Lab
mechanicsByNeed.why: Errors are bounded, depersonalised, analysed and converted into recovery strategies and future action.
